original_value: SummaryMany non‐homogeneous Poisson process software reliability growth models (SRGM) are characterized by a single continuous curve. However, failures are driven by factors such as the testing strategy and environment, integration testing and resource allocation, which can introduce one or more changepoint into the fault detection process. Some researchers have proposed non‐homogeneous Poisson process SRGM, but only consider a common failure distribution before and after changepoints. This paper proposes a heterogeneous single changepoint framework for SRGM, which can exhibit different failure distributions before and after the changepoint. Combinations of two simple and distinct curves including an exponential and S‐shaped curve are employed to illustrate the concept. Ten data sets are used to compare these heterogeneous models against their homogeneous counterparts. Experimental results indicate that heterogeneous changepoint models achieve better goodness‐of‐fit measures on 60% and 80% of the data sets with respect to the Akaike information criterion and predictive sum of squares measures.

result.paraphrase: Many non-homogeneous Poisson process software reliability growth models (SRGM) are represented by a single continuous curve. Yet failures are influenced by factors such as the testing strategy and environment, integration testing, and resource allocation, which can introduce one or more changepoints in the fault detection process. Some researchers have proposed non-homogeneous Poisson process SRGM, but these only assume a common failure distribution before and after changepoints. This paper introduces a heterogeneous single-changepoint framework for SRGM, allowing different failure distributions before and after the changepoint. To illustrate the idea, combinations of two simple and distinct curves, including exponential and S-shaped curves, are used. Ten data sets are employed to compare these heterogeneous models with their homogeneous counterparts. Experimental results show that the heterogeneous changepoint models provide better goodness-of-fit on 60% and 80% of the data sets according to the Akaike information criterion and predictive sum of squares measures.
